title: Econometrics
tagline: Economic data, simple and multiple regression, inference, functional form and specification, heteroskedasticity, binary outcomes, panel data and instrumental variables
summary: Econometrics uses data to measure economic relationships and test economic theories. This course develops linear regression from first principles — estimation by ordinary least squares, its statistical properties, hypothesis tests and confidence intervals — and then the tools that real data demand: functional form and dummy variables, heteroskedasticity and robust inference, models for binary outcomes, panel data and instrumental variables. Probability and statistical inference are reviewed briefly; their full treatment is in the Maths Atlas.

chapters.title: Economic data and the aims of econometrics
chapters.summary: Cross-section, time-series and panel data, correlation versus causation, and a review of the probability and statistics used in the course.

chapters.title: The simple regression model
chapters.summary: Ordinary least squares with one regressor, its algebraic properties, goodness of fit and the interpretation of coefficients.

chapters.title: Multiple regression
chapters.summary: OLS with several regressors in matrix form, partialling out, omitted-variable bias and the Gauss–Markov theorem.

chapters.title: Inference in regression
chapters.summary: Sampling distributions of OLS estimators, t and F tests, confidence intervals and large-sample inference.

chapters.title: Functional form, dummy variables and specification
chapters.summary: Logarithms, quadratics and interactions, qualitative regressors, and tests of model specification.

chapters.title: Heteroskedasticity and robust inference
chapters.summary: Consequences of heteroskedasticity, robust and clustered standard errors, and weighted least squares.

chapters.title: Binary outcomes: linear probability, probit and logit
chapters.summary: Models for yes-or-no outcomes, maximum likelihood estimation and the interpretation of marginal effects.

chapters.title: Panel data
chapters.summary: Pooled, first-difference, fixed-effects and random-effects estimators for repeated observations of the same units.

chapters.title: Endogeneity and instrumental variables
chapters.summary: Measurement error, simultaneity and omitted variables, instrumental variables and two-stage least squares.
